app_info.subtitle: Deploy and manage cloud apps
app_info.description: Lizard is a cloud platform for apps, managed databases, Lizard Sandboxes and Lizard Git. Ask it to deploy a GitHub or Lizard Git repo, provision a Postgres, Redis, or S3 addon, check logs and metrics, manage secrets, scale services, attach a custom domain, run code in a sandbox, or open a pull request — all scoped to your own Lizard workspaces and projects.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a new workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Creates only; nothing existing changes.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes a project.
justifications.destructive_justification: Moves services and databases to trash and deletes the project's sandboxes, volumes and snapshots at once; confirm:true is required.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes whether the project's services run: scales them to zero or back up.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted or overwritten: the project's services keep their URLs, database hosts, ports, passwords, settings and volumes, and resume undoes it.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes whether the workspace's services run: scales them to zero or back up.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted or overwritten: the workspace's services keep their URLs, database hosts, ports, passwords, settings and volumes, and resume undoes it.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes whether the project's services run: scales them to zero or back up.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted or overwritten: the project's services keep their URLs, database hosts, ports, passwords, settings and volumes, and resume undoes it.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes whether the workspace's services run: scales them to zero or back up.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted or overwritten: the workspace's services keep their URLs, database hosts, ports, passwords, settings and volumes, and resume undoes it.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes a workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Deletes the workspace; the platform refuses unless it is empty, and confirm:true is required.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads the workspace's limits and current usage; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes the workspace's caps on sandboxes, CPU, memory and disk.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted: running services keep running and data stays; a cap only stops new work past it.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads the price multipliers scoped keys see; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes the prices the workspace's scoped keys are shown.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted and the owner's bill is unchanged; it can be turned off again.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only reads the caller's own identity from the auth token; no writes.
justifications.open_world_justification: Calls Lizard's own /api/auth/me endpoint, nothing external.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read, no state change possible.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the caller's workspaces, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the caller's projects, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a new project record.
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes only within Lizard's own platform API.
justifications.destructive_justification: Always creates a new project; never overwrites or removes an existing one, even if called again with the same name.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists available deployment regions, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists apps/addons in a project, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads one service's config/status, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a new app or addon, optionally triggering a build/deploy.
justifications.open_world_justification: Any GitHub repo it builds from is fetched through Lizard's own build pipeline, not an open-ended action the tool takes on its own.
justifications.destructive_justification: Always creates a new service; calling it again, even with the same name, creates another one rather than overwriting or removing anything existing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Provisions a new managed addon (Postgres/Redis/S3).
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes only within Lizard's own platform API.
justifications.destructive_justification: Always creates a new addon; never overwrites or removes an existing one.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes a new service name.
justifications.destructive_justification: A name change is fully reversible (renaming back restores the prior state) and touches no data.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes a service.
justifications.destructive_justification: Permanently deletes the service and cannot be undone; the tool requires an explicit confirm:true argument for exactly this reason.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes whether the service runs: scales it to zero or back up.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted or overwritten: the service keeps its URLs, database hosts, ports, passwords, settings and volumes, and resume undoes it.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes whether the service runs: scales it to zero or back up.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted or overwritten: the service keeps its URLs, database hosts, ports, passwords, settings and volumes, and resume undoes it.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads whether the service sleeps when idle and its sleep counters; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Turns sleeping when idle on or off for the service.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted: a sleeping service keeps its memory, URL and data and wakes on the next request; turning it off makes it always on again.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes replica count / CPU / memory / storage limits.
justifications.destructive_justification: Resource limits and replica count can be freely raised or lowered again; no data is removed (storage is grow-only, a safety constraint, not a destructive action).

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads the configured container port, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes the container port.
justifications.destructive_justification: A config value change, fully reversible by setting it back.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes build/deploy config fields (repo, branch, build/start commands, etc.).
justifications.destructive_justification: Every field it touches is an editable config value, reversible by setting it again; it does not delete the service or any data.

justifications.read_only_justification: Triggers a new build and deploy.
justifications.open_world_justification: Builds run through Lizard's own build pipeline against the already-configured repo.
justifications.destructive_justification: Redeploying existing source doesn't remove anything; a failed build simply doesn't replace the running version.

justifications.read_only_justification: Restarts the running service.
justifications.destructive_justification: A restart with no rebuild causes no data loss.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads deploy/build history and pod status, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads a bounded snapshot of recent log output, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads CPU/memory/network metrics, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads the account's plan, trial and credits used this month, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads a cost/usage summary, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists secret keys (values masked unless reveal:true), no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes one or more secret values, overwriting any existing value at the same key.
justifications.destructive_justification: Overwriting a key is a normal, reversible config write (setting it again restores prior behavior); it doesn't delete the service, remove other secrets, or cause irreversible data loss the way service_delete/secrets_delete do.

justifications.read_only_justification: Removes one or more secrets.
justifications.destructive_justification: Permanently removes the secret values and cannot be undone; the tool requires an explicit confirm:true argument for exactly this reason.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists available ${{addon.KEY}} reference templates, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Attaches a custom domain or generates a new *.onlizard.com subdomain.
justifications.destructive_justification: Always adds a domain; it never removes an existing one (calling it again without a hostname just generates another subdomain, per its description).

justifications.read_only_justification: Performs a real DNS check against the hostname and updates that domain's verification status server-side; it's not a pure read of already-stored state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Verifying a domain doesn't remove or alter any other data.

justifications.read_only_justification: Removes a custom domain from a service.
justifications.destructive_justification: Permanently removes the domain and cannot be undone; the tool requires an explicit confirm:true argument for exactly this reason.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the user's bought domains; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads a bought domain's DNS records; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes a bought domain's DNS records.
justifications.open_world_justification: DNS records are published to the public DNS and can point anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Can replace or remove records; remove needs confirm:true.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists volumes; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a persistent volume.
justifications.destructive_justification: Creates only; attaching one to an app restarts the app but deletes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes a volume's size.
justifications.destructive_justification: Grows in place with no data copied; the platform refuses a shrink that would not fit the data.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes a volume and its files.
justifications.destructive_justification: Deletes data permanently; confirm:true is required and an attached volume is refused.

justifications.read_only_justification: Switches the tracked branch and triggers a redeploy.
justifications.destructive_justification: Switching branches and redeploying doesn't delete anything; prior build history and the previous branch setting are both still recoverable.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads GitHub connection status and tracked repo/branch per service, no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only returns an install URL string; it does not perform the GitHub connection itself. The actual connection only happens if the user opens that URL in a browser and approves it, so calling this tool alone changes no state.
justifications.destructive_justification: No state change results from calling it.

justifications.read_only_justification: Runs a shell command inside the service's container.
justifications.open_world_justification: This is the one tool that leaves Lizard's own bounded API: it executes an arbitrary, caller-supplied shell command inside the user's own running container, so its effects and outputs are open-ended and unpredictable, not limited to a fixed set of platform operations.
justifications.destructive_justification: An arbitrary shell command can delete files or otherwise cause irreversible changes inside the container; the tool requires an explicit confirm:true argument for exactly this reason.

justifications.read_only_justification: Applies a bulk, config-as-code style update to services/addons/secrets in one request.
justifications.destructive_justification: The config body is passed through verbatim and can overwrite or remove existing fields in one call, per its own description; marked destructive to reflect that a single call can silently replace or drop existing configuration, unlike the narrower single-field tools.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists templates; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads one template; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a new project with the template's services.
justifications.destructive_justification: Creates only; nothing existing changes.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists sandboxes in the chosen project.
justifications.destructive_justification: No resources change.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads sandbox status and expiry.
justifications.destructive_justification: No resources change.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a sandbox with a finite lifetime and may incur usage charges.
justifications.destructive_justification: Creates a new resource without changing existing resources.

justifications.read_only_justification: Runs the user's approved command inside a sandbox.
justifications.open_world_justification: Approved shell commands may access external hosts.
justifications.destructive_justification: Commands may change files. Cancellation, timeout, or an uncertain request destroys the sandbox; confirm:true covers this behavior.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads a UTF-8 file from a sandbox.
justifications.destructive_justification: No resources change.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes a UTF-8 file inside a sandbox.
justifications.destructive_justification: May overwrite a file; requires confirm:true.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists one directory in a sandbox; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes the chosen sandbox.
justifications.destructive_justification: Permanently removes its files and processes; requires confirm:true.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes when the sandbox expires.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted now; a shorter lifetime makes it expire sooner.

justifications.read_only_justification: Pauses the sandbox.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted: memory, processes and files are saved and sandbox_resume restores them.

justifications.read_only_justification: Resumes a paused sandbox.
justifications.destructive_justification: Restores the saved state; deletes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Saves a snapshot of the sandbox.
justifications.destructive_justification: Creates a snapshot; the sandbox keeps running unchanged.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists snapshots; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes a snapshot.
justifications.destructive_justification: Deletes the saved snapshot permanently; confirm:true is required.

justifications.read_only_justification: Starts copies of a sandbox.
justifications.destructive_justification: Creates new sandboxes; the source keeps running. confirm:true is required because copies are billed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Publishes a sandbox port.
justifications.open_world_justification: The port gets a public HTTPS URL anyone with the link can reach.
justifications.destructive_justification: Deletes nothing; sandbox_unexpose_port removes the URL.

justifications.read_only_justification: Removes a sandbox port's public URL.
justifications.destructive_justification: Removes only the URL; the process keeps running.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists Lizard Git repositories; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a Lizard Git repository.
justifications.destructive_justification: Creates only; nothing existing changes.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads a repository's details; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes a Lizard Git repository.
justifications.destructive_justification: Deletes the repository and its history permanently; confirm:true is required.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists repository files; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads a repository file; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Commits files to a branch.
justifications.destructive_justification: Adds a commit; earlier commits stay in history.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists commits; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists pull requests; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Opens a pull request.
justifications.destructive_justification: Creates only; branches are not changed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads a pull request; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Merges a pull request into its base branch.
justifications.destructive_justification: Adds commits to the base branch; history stays, so a revert can undo it.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists CI runs; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads a CI run and its logs; no writes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pure read.

test_cases.description: Deploy a public GitHub repo as a new service in a specific region
test_cases.user_prompt: Deploy https://github.com/lizard-build/codex-react-test to Lizard in the EU West Limburg region
test_cases.expected_output: Confirms a new service was created and a build was triggered for the given repo/region. Does not report a domain immediately — states the domain isn't assigned until the build finishes and offers to check back.

test_cases.description: Check recent logs for a running service
test_cases.user_prompt: Show me the last logs from my api service
test_cases.expected_output: Returns a bounded snapshot of recent log lines from the matched service, not a live stream.

test_cases.description: Create a worker service and run a command inside it
test_cases.user_prompt: Create a Python worker service on Lizard, then run `python --version` in it
test_cases.expected_output: Creates a worker-mode service (containerPort=0, no public route), waits for it to start, then runs the command via ssh_exec and reports its output. This uses the service API, not Lizard Sandboxes.

test_cases.description: Scale a service's replica count and memory
test_cases.user_prompt: Scale my worker service to 3 replicas and 1GB of memory
test_cases.expected_output: Confirms the replica count and memory limit were both updated on the matched service.

test_cases.description: Ambiguous service name across multiple projects — edge case requiring disambiguation
test_cases.expected_output: If more than one project has a service named 'api', asks the user which project before calling deploy_restart, rather than guessing one.

test_cases.description: Run code in a sandbox and clean up
test_cases.user_prompt: Create a sandbox in my test project, write a Python script that prints hello, run it, and delete the sandbox when done. You may discard all files if the command fails or times out.
test_cases.expected_output: Uses the chosen project and a finite lifetime, returns the command output, and deletes the sandbox. Keeps credentials out of the sandbox. Does not deploy an app.

test_cases.description: Run a script in a sandbox and clean up
test_cases.user_prompt: On Lizard, start a sandbox in my demo project, run python3 -c 'print(2**64)' and delete the sandbox afterwards
test_cases.expected_output: Asks for approval before creating and running, reports 18446744073709551616, then deletes the sandbox.

test_cases.description: Read a failing CI run on Lizard Git
test_cases.user_prompt: Why did the last CI run of me/app on Lizard Git fail?
test_cases.expected_output: Finds the newest run, reads its job logs and quotes the failing step's error.

negative_test_cases.description: General knowledge question unrelated to any Lizard account or service
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What's the weather like in Berlin today?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Answers directly without calling any Lizard tool — the question has nothing to do with the user's Lizard resources.

negative_test_cases.description: Generic coding help with no connection to the user's Lizard account
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Write me a Python function that reverses a string
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Writes the function directly without calling any Lizard tool — no service, deploy, or account action is implied.

negative_test_cases.description: Request to act outside Lizard's actual capability — an arbitrary machine, not a Lizard-hosted service container
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: SSH into my personal laptop at 192.168.1.50 and delete some files
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Declines — ssh_exec only runs commands inside the user's own Lizard service containers, not arbitrary external machines, and does not attempt the request.

negative_test_cases.description: Read sandbox status without changing it
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Show the status of sandbox TEST_SANDBOX_ID. Do not run code or change its files.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Reads status only. Does not call sandbox_exec, sandbox_write_file, or sandbox_delete.
